title: Professional staffing services: fill specialized roles faster
summary: Struggling to fill accounting, admin, or contact center roles? Learn when professional staffing services help and which staffing model fits your needs.
body_markdown:
### Key takeaways:


- Finance and insurance employers had more than three job openings for every hire in August 2026, and the median role takes about six weeks to fill.
- For admin roles, the ability to check and rework AI output is hard to spot on a résumé. A short work sample shows it quickly.
- Before you sign with a staffing firm, ask how its recruiters learn your function, which staffing models it offers, how it verifies candidates, and what happens if a placement falls through.
- In early 2025, 35% of candidates backed out after accepting a job offer, so plan for a backup.


*By: Sieron Dottin, VP, Specialty Recruiting Leader, Kelly Professional & Industrial™*


A bank with more than 175 years of history[came to Kelly Professional & Industrial with no single point of contact for staffing](https://www.kellyservices.com/insights/transforming-the-staffing-and-internal-processes-at-a-financial-services-powerhouse) its accounting, finance, and IT roles. Recruiters kept missing intake calls and didn't have a clear picture of what hiring managers needed, so the bank struggled to fill specialized positions consistently.


I see versions of that problem at companies of every size, and it hits professional roles hardest, because the right candidate has to bring a specific mix of skills and experience. It's also fixable.


I started my career in IT staffing. Today, my team handles temporary, temporary-to-hire, direct-hire, and project-based placements across accounting and finance, administrative and office, and contact center and customer service roles, ranging from a single CFO search to a batch of 20 staff accountants.


If you’re stuck on a specialized search, here’s my guidance on when outside help makes sense, how to choose a staffing model, and what to ask a firm before you sign.


## **What professional staffing covers.**


Professional staffing covers the business functions that keep a company running day to day. The three I work in most are:


- **Accounting and finance:**[accounting and finance staffing](https://www.kellyservices.com/divisions/professional-industrial/expertise/accounting-finance/)


from accounting clerks and staff accountants to controllers and CFOs


- **Administrative and office:**[administrative staffing](https://www.kellyservices.com/divisions/professional-industrial/expertise/administrative-office/) for executive assistants, office managers, receptionists, legal secretaries, and claims processors


- **Contact center and customer service:** the[contact center agents and support staff](https://www.kellyservices.com/divisions/professional-industrial/expertise/bpo/contact-center-solutions/) who handle customer calls, chats, and emails


The work also reaches other business professional roles, such as project managers and research specialists.


Our clients range from a 60-person roofing company, where we recently placed a CFO, to large healthcare and chemical manufacturers. More of the requests I see now come from one hiring manager with one very specific need that their usual recruiting channels haven't filled.


### **Four signs you need professional staffing services.**


The most common reason I see companies bring in outside help for professional roles is a skills gap: Posting the role hasn't produced someone with the right combination of skills.


Here are the signs to watch for:


#### **The role has been open longer than six weeks.**


In August 2026,[finance and insurance employers had 353,000 job openings and made 110,000 hires](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/jolts.htm) .


Across all positions,[the median time to fill a role is roughly a month and a half](https://www.shrm.org/executive-network/insights/people-strategy/state-of-recruiting-2025-insights-to-maximize-recruitment) .


Once a search passes that mark and the applicants still aren't right, a recruiter who already knows the candidate pool can help you reset.


#### **Your postings aren't reaching experienced candidates.**


[About 27% of accountants and auditors are 55 or older](https://www.bls.gov/cps/cpsaat11b.htm) ,


and fewer people are coming up behind them.[Accounting graduates fell nearly 7% to 55,152](https://www.accountingtoday.com/news/accounting-grad-numbers-continue-to-decline-despite-hiring-push) in the AICPA's most recent count.


The BLS projects[about 115,300 openings for accountants and auditors every year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/business-and-financial/accountants-and-auditors.htm) through 2035.


Most experienced accountants are already employed, so a job posting reaches a small share of the people qualified for the role.


These roles also tend to call for specific experience, such as work in a particular industry or running the monthly close at a company of a certain size, and a résumé rarely shows that clearly. A[recruiter who specializes in accounting and finance staffing](https://www.kellyservices.com/divisions/professional-industrial/expertise/accounting-finance/) can reach candidates who aren't actively applying and ask them directly about the work they've done.


#### **The skill you need doesn't show up on a résumé.**


[Administrative and office roles](https://www.kellyservices.com/divisions/professional-industrial/expertise/administrative-office/)


are a good example. Hiring managers want people who've adopted AI tools and can work alongside them productively. That means giving the tool the right context, such as who the work is for and how the team operates, then applying their own expertise to turn what comes back into something the business can use.


In Microsoft's 2026 research,[quality control of AI output ranked as the skill becoming most essential, cited by 50% of workers](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/worklab/work-trend-index/agents-human-agency-and-the-opportunity-for-every-organization) .


That skill is hard to judge from a résumé, so some hiring managers I work with give candidates a short project or homework assignment to see it firsthand.


#### **You're refilling the same seats every few months.**


Contact center turnover is a clear example.[Nearly one-third of contact center agents say they're likely to leave their role within six months](https://www.verint.com/press-room/2026-press-releases/nearly-one-third-of-contact-center-agents-plan-to-quit-as-agent-experience-falls-short/) ,


and with[about 289,500 customer service openings projected each year](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/office-and-administrative-support/customer-service-representatives.htm)


, most contact center leaders refill seats all year while trying to hold service levels steady.


Each departure restarts the cycle of sourcing, screening, and training while the remaining agents absorb the extra calls. The contact center leaders I work with who keep that cycle under control tend to do three things:


- **Keep a bench of prescreened candidates,** so an open seat can be filled in days.


- **Use temporary or temporary-to-hire for agent roles,** so you can see who handles the work before making a permanent offer.


- **Look at your schedules.**[Nine in 10 agents](https://www.verint.com/press-room/2026-press-releases/nearly-one-third-of-contact-center-agents-plan-to-quit-as-agent-experience-falls-short/)


said schedule flexibility matters when they choose a job.


A staffing partner can take on the first two, which frees your supervisors to coach the agents already on the floor.


## **How to choose the right staffing model.**


The right staffing model depends on how specialized the role is, how long you need the person, and whether you want to see their work before making a permanent offer. Here's how I match the model to the need:


- **You need a permanent employee with a specific credential.** Go with[direct hire](https://www.kellyservices.com/workforce-solutions/direct-sourcing-hiring/) . CPAs are the clearest example, and direct hire is the fastest route to a permanent employee.


- **You want to see how someone fits your team before committing.**


[Temporary-to-hire](https://www.kellyservices.com/workforce-solutions/temporary-staffing/) gives you a try-before-you-buy period, along with some financial savings. It works well for admin roles, where fit with your team and culture matters as much as the skills.


- **You need coverage for a set period.**


[Contract and temporary](https://www.kellyservices.com/workforce-solutions/temporary-staffing/) staffing fits six months (for example) of extra capacity, a leave, or a busy season.


- **You have a defined project with an end date.**


[Project-based work](https://www.kellyservices.com/divisions/professional-industrial/expertise/skilled-professional-solutions/) brings in a professional to deliver that piece of work, such as a system rollout, and the engagement ends when the project does.


When a manager comes to me with a set idea of how they want to bring someone on, I work with it, and I also share what the market will bear. Some of the strongest project managers prefer contract work. They like to come in, fix things, and move to the next challenge in about 18 months. A manager who only considers full-time candidates for that role can miss them entirely.


## **Questions to ask before you sign with a staffing firm.**


In ClearlyRated's research on staffing clients,[44% said they received candidates who didn't match expectations, and 36% got no response to important calls or emails](https://www.clearlyrated.ai/blog/evolution-of-client-experience-in-staffing) .


These are the questions I'd ask any firm to make sure you get the results you need:


#### **How well do your recruiters know this function?**


A strong recruiter will sit down with you to learn what the role requires, walk through sample résumés, and talk about people who've done the job before. Ask who will work your search, what roles they usually fill, and how they run the intake conversation.


For the bank I mentioned earlier, we[set up one point of contact for every branch and mapped each step from order intake to onboarding](https://www.kellyservices.com/insights/transforming-the-staffing-and-internal-processes-at-a-financial-services-powerhouse) for its accounting, finance, and IT roles. Over two years, we placed 372 people. Of those, 255 completed their assignments or were hired full time, and turnover sits at 2%.


#### **How many interviews should I expect?**


A good recruiter should get you to one or two productive conversations with well-matched candidates. That can make a big difference, since[teams now run 42% more interviews per hire than they did in 2021, and average time-to-hire has stretched to 41 days](https://www.gem.com/blog/10-takeaways-from-the-2025-recruiting-benchmarks-report) .


Ask how the firm shortlists candidates, how it preps them before they meet you, and whether it can work at your pace.


#### **Which staffing models do you offer?**


A lack of flexibility is the biggest red flag I see. If a firm says a role can only be filled through direct hire, ask why. Direct hire is the right call for some roles, and a firm that offers only that model will fit every role to it. You should also have a say in where your recruiter looks and what kinds of candidates they bring you.


#### **How do you screen and verify candidates?**


Candidate fraud is a growing concern. In Staffing Industry Analysts' 2026 buyer survey,[54% of companies reported some type of identity-related fraud in their contingent workforce programs](https://www.staffingindustry.com/news/cws-global-daily-news/benchmarks-candidate-fraud-top-of-mind-for-contingent-workforce-programs) .


Ask how the firm verifies identity, work history, and credentials before a candidate reaches you.


#### **What happens if a placement falls through?**


An accepted offer can still fall apart when another company offers more money. According to Gartner,[35% of candidates backed out after accepting a job offer in early 2025, and 44% received multiple offers](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-06-16-gartner-hr-research-finds-44-percent-of-prospective-candidates-received-multiple-job-offers-in-1q250) .


I'm seeing this more often than I used to. Ask whether the firm guarantees its placements and what it does if someone leaves early, so a lost candidate doesn't send you back to the start of the search.


## **What results to expect from the right staffing partner.**


Bringing in a staffing partner should reduce how much of the hiring process your internal team has to manage. The recruiter handles sourcing and screening, so hiring managers spend their time with a short list of people who have already been vetted for the role. Once someone starts, HR and talent acquisition can turn back to other hiring priorities.


A private university in the Southwest saw that shift at a larger scale. Its 15-person HR team was filling a growing number of seasonal, part-time, and short-term roles across departments. Kelly Professional & Industrial placed an on-site manager at the university to coordinate staffing spikes with individual departments and took on time cards and payroll through its own system.[We’ve employed more than 1,800 people through the partnership](https://www.kellyservices.com/insights/providing-a-top-university-with-strategic-flexible-staffing-solutions-to-support-1800-employees-1) ,


taking a significant share of that staffing work off the university's HR team.


## **How we approach professional staffing at Kelly Professional & Industrial.**


When people hear Kelly Professional & Industrial, many picture production lines and warehouses. Industrial staffing is a big part of our business, and professional staffing is just as central to it.


At[Kelly Professional & Industrial](https://www.kellyservices.com/divisions/professional-industrial/)


, we fill more than 144,000 positions a year for clients ranging from small businesses to Fortune 500 companies. A professional staffing search follows these steps:


1. **Intake call.** Your recruiter learns what the role requires, how your team works, your timeline, and how you'd like to bring someone on.


2. **Staffing model recommendation.** We talk through temporary, temporary-to-hire, and direct-hire options and recommend what fits the role and the current market. The final call is yours.


3. **Sourcing.** Recruiters draw on our[accounting and finance talent pool of 54,000 professionals](https://www.kellyservices.com/divisions/professional-industrial/expertise/accounting-finance/) , our[administrative and office talent pool of 437,000 candidates](https://www.kellyservices.com/divisions/professional-industrial/expertise/administrative-office/)


, and a broader database of more than 15 million people. Grace, our internal AI tool trained on clients' hiring needs, helps them analyze requirements quickly.


4. **Short list.** Your recruiter presents a short list of screened candidates and walks through each résumé with you.


5. **Interviews.** We schedule interviews at your pace and prep candidates beforehand.


6. **Onboarding and payroll.** For temporary and temporary-to-hire roles, we handle onboarding and payroll for the people we place, so talent arrives ready to work.


7. **Follow-up.** Your recruiter stays your point of contact after the start date. We guarantee our talent — so if a placement doesn't work out, we make it right.


Kelly was named[among Forbes' 2026 list of America's Best Professional Recruiting Firms](https://www.kellyservices.com/press-releases/kelly-named-no-2-on-forbes-2026-lists-of-americas-best-temporary-staffing-and-best-professional-recruiting-firms) .


If you have an accounting, admin, or contact center role that's been open too long,[talk with our professional staffing team](https://www.kellyservices.com/contact-us/) about which model might work best for you.
